newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Congress to rule on euthanasia.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Congress to rule on euthanasia.

text.p: Colombia's Congress will be asked to set the terms under which euthanasia, legalised by the Constitutional Court in a landmark ruling last week, can be carried out, a court member said on Tuesday.

"At this time it has become more necessary than ever...to legislate with respect to the problem of dignified death," court magistrate Carlos Gaviria, a leading proponent of euthanasia, told reporters.

He said that while the court decriminalized euthanasia in its ruling last Tuesday, lawmakers -- and not the court -- should decide exactly how doctors proceeded in cases involving terminally-ill patients who asked to die themselves.
A poll published in Bogota's El Espectador newspaper this month, shortly before the court ruling, showed that most Colombians support the legalisation of euthanasia.

But the ruling, striking down mandatory prison sentences of six months to three years for anyone responsible for the practice, nevertheless sparked a storm of controversy in the predominantly Roman Catholic country.

Gino Concetti, a Roman Catholic theologian, said last week he hoped Congress would overturn the ruling just as Australia's did after the world's first euthanasia law was passed by the Northern Territory government in July 1996.
